characters.description: A returning human mage who reaches a human city with Terry while an iron Doskanok runs through her body. She removes Kit and leaves it outside a cleansing circle before entering an emergency teleportation procedure intended to separate her from the creature.
characters.name: Tala

characters.description: An iron creature threaded through Tala's body when she reaches human territory. Its presence prompts an urgent cleansing teleport intended to separate it from her.
characters.name: Iron Doskanok

characters.description: Tala's intelligent terror-bird companion, capable of flicker-teleporting and changing his apparent size. He reunites with her outside a human city and accompanies her to the urgent cleansing procedure.
characters.name: Terry

characters.description: Tala's named dimensional storage and mobile refuge. Before she enters the cleansing circle, she removes Kit with her other non-soulbound possessions and leaves it outside the procedure.
characters.name: Kit

characters.description: An unnamed paragon stationed at Aelfast Waning. When Tala arrives with an iron Doskanok throughout her body, he assumes charge of a teleportation-based attempt to purge it.
characters.name: Human paragon

characters.description: A cooperative mental perspective sharing Tala's body. Alat falls silent when the cleansing teleport strips away Tala's inscriptions, then returns after Tala uses Kit to restore them.
characters.name: Alat

characters.description: Rain's older brother, an underpowered mage who depends on a draining dark-crystal staff for his magical development. He greets Tala and Terry with hostility before becoming formally polite.
characters.name: Rain's older brother

characters.description: A longtime human friend of Tala who joins the local paragon in sheltering her after her changed power unsettles nearby people.
characters.name: Rain

characters.description: A returning friend of Tala and her contact in the Caravan Guild who welcomes her return.
characters.name: Lynn

characters.description: Tala's thirteen-year-old sibling and a second-year academy student. Her magical education emphasizes combat, and a birthday message brings confirmation that Tala survived.
characters.name: Illie

characters.description: An archivist and trusted information broker who reviews material sent by Tala. She verifies Tala's captivity, confirms that human authorities know of the situation, and arranges to support her arrival in Banfast.
characters.name: Ingrit

characters.description: A lead inscriptionist and refining specialist present at Tala's return briefing. Her first examination identifies Tala's condition as dangerously unstable and establishes the need for careful stabilization.
characters.name: Holly

characters.description: A senior human mage and adviser who brings Tala and Rain into Banfast without public notice. He delivers them to the formal Archon briefing arranged around Tala's return.
characters.name: Grediv

characters.description: A Constructionist Guild master whose own bodily deterioration resembles the regeneration damage threatening Tala. His condition is raised as a relevant comparison during the first assessment of her instability.
characters.name: Jevin

characters.description: A concealed Reforged who supports controlled study of an inactive automaton because the Black Legion may be stirring. Tala detects him with void sight, and he indicates that they will speak later.
characters.name: Hidden Reforged

characters.description: A Constructionist Guild master admitted to the restricted portion of Tala's return briefing. Boma is cleared to remain while the group examines sensitive arcane knowledge and recovered materials.
characters.name: Boma

characters.description: A Constructionist Guild master admitted to Tala's restricted briefing. Q remains with the small group authorized to examine Kit and other sensitive discoveries brought back to Banfast.
characters.name: Q

characters.description: An artificial personality organized around a fount but distinct from it. Rob asks to stop existing, while the associated fount makes a different choice, forcing Banfast's council to consider them separately.
characters.name: Rob

characters.description: Lynn's mageling, who manages work around Lynn's household. The mageling is part of Tala's renewed circle in Banfast but is introduced without a reliably established personal name.
characters.name: Lynn's mageling

characters.description: The head of the Banfast Archon Council, who joins the assessment of Kit and uses a purpose-built diagnostic orb to examine its dimensional condition.
characters.name: Banfast Archon Council head

characters.description: A senior Archon trained to treat psychological harm caused by magical unions and similar events. He meets Tala inside Kit, recognizes her habit of separating herself from others, and sets expectations for honest but voluntary discussion.
characters.name: Trauma therapist

characters.description: A mage hunter who tracks a thief through magical sensor nets, manipulates magnetic fields and iron, and disables the thief's keystone during the arrest.
characters.name: Cazor

characters.description: Tala's elderly former overseer in the Caravan Guild. Nearing death, she has arranged for her fount to be released from Zeme and declines Tala's offer of continued existence as a mind bound to it.
characters.name: Tala's former caravan overseer

characters.description: An Archon whom Tala consults about creatures that reinforce reality, unstable regions beyond ordinary space, and advanced magic. He explains how such creatures stabilize Zeme and how the strongest can endanger anything within the area they affect.
characters.name: Expert Archon

characters.description: A constructionist proposed as an assistant for Tala's mobile sanctum. Simon and his family are considering a household arrangement that would place his technical expertise inside Kit.
characters.name: Simon

characters.description: Simon's wife and a member of the family considering relocation into Kit with their three youngest children.
characters.name: Petra

characters.description: A senior Constructionist Guild specialist assigned to examine Tala's altered weapon. She finds that its new forms carry a power that changes who owns iron.
characters.name: Senior constructionist

characters.description: The constructionist who delivers the morphic sheath made for Tala's weapon. The fitted sheath changes with the weapon's forms and diffuses the force of its impacts.
characters.name: Mistress Aram

characters.description: A returning acquaintance from Tala's guard-training days. Their guarded reunion makes clear that her power and combat history have placed lasting distance between them, and both expect it may be their final meeting.
characters.name: Adam

characters.description: An unidentified elderly mage whom Tala finds alone in a stable, low-magic dell. He is unresponsive and irreversibly entering the fugue that precedes becoming a fount, so Tala remains to witness the transformation.
characters.name: Elderly mage

characters.description: Tala's estranged parent and the proprietor of the family alchemist shop in Marleyweather. He waits outside Tala's childhood home when she finally arrives to face a difficult family reunion.
characters.name: Tala's father

characters.description: Tala's oldest sister, an alchemist studying magical theory under a healer-mage. She meets Tala during the siblings' reunion and discusses a possible path toward receiving a keystone and inscriptions.
characters.name: Tala's eldest sister

characters.description: An unnamed healer-mage who teaches magical theory to Tala's eldest sister and expects that she may eventually be ready for a keystone and basic inscriptions.
characters.name: Healer-mage

characters.description: Two of Tala's younger siblings, both twelve and determined to attend the academy. They listen to her honest account of mage work and remain committed despite its dangers.
characters.name: Tala's academy-bound twins

characters.description: A magical predator newly occupying a mountain valley rich in founts. It attacks Tala, draws enormous strength from the terrain, and rapidly restores even severe physical damage.
characters.name: Upland tiger

recaps.ending: Tala closes the volume as a Refined mage who is relocating her base from Banfast to the city where Rain is based. Her iron bond has been joined to her soulbound weapon, giving her formidable defenses with limits that Cazor continues to test. Terry remains beside her to explore a flock partnership, without accepting a soul bond. Simon, Petra, and their family are building a working home within Kit, though internal teleportation remains unsolved. Tala has renewed ties with her siblings and watched the twins leave for the academy, but she gives no answer to her father's offer of future support. Banfast still holds Rob and five founts, Tala retains an inactive automaton for study, and the nature of founts, the dome, void, and the next world remains unsettled. An upland tiger also survives in its valley after driving Tala and Terry away. Tala retains friends and collaborators in Banfast and plans to visit them after establishing herself in her new base.
recaps.in_short: Tala returns to human territory carrying an iron Doskanok that cannot be removed, so she negotiates a soul bond with it. Back in Banfast, she shares intelligence from captivity, confronts and integrates the false identity imposed on her, ends her Caravan Guild obligations, and prepares for refinement. Holly helps merge the unstable iron bond into Tala's weapon, and Tala survives a painful transformation into a Refined mage. Kit becomes a staffed mobile home for Simon, Petra, and their family. Tala later witnesses a mage become a fount and sends it onward through a dangerous encounter spanning Zeme, a mysterious dome, and the next world. She reconnects with her siblings in Marleyweather, leaves reconciliation with her parents unresolved, and supports the academy-bound twins' departure. Terry chooses to remain and attempt a true flock partnership. After retreating from an upland tiger, Tala returns to Banfast, tests her iron defenses with Cazor, and prepares to relocate to the city where Rain is based.

recaps.text: Previously: Tala is a human mage who travels with Terry, an intelligent terror-bird capable of crossing space in sudden flickers. She also keeps Kit, a named dimensional refuge that carries her possessions and serves as a mobile shelter. Their unusual partnership and Tala's accumulated magical bonds shape the condition in which she begins this volume.

Tala reaches a human city with an iron Doskanok threaded through her body and asks a human paragon to remove it through a repeating teleportation. The process burns away her exterior iron and strips her inscriptions, but the creature resists separation and begins forcing a bond. Tala rejects the destructive selves it offers and negotiates control over her own iron, power, and identity. She survives with the Doskanok soulbound to her, then restores her inscriptions from Kit. The bond lets her claim iron she owns, draw it into her body, and reinforce her magic, but it also affects nearby mundanes and produces a severe hunger. Tala tells the paragon about her abduction, erased memories, service to the House of Blood, and escape after killing her controller. Rain reunites with her, and they leave for Banfast with Terry and the paragon. Illie and Ingrit learn that Tala is alive. During the journey Tala tries sealing herself in bonded iron, causing catastrophic magical overload and internal injury. She survives, but any deeper union with the iron must wait until refinement and careful testing.

Tala discovers that repeated errors in her regenerated body will eventually become fatal unless she refines or finds another repair. Grediv brings her and Rain into Banfast, where Lynn, Ingrit, Holly, and other specialists receive her. A tiered briefing confirms her captivity, her forced service as a House of Blood enforcer, and the collar attack that injected the iron Doskanok after she killed her controller. Tala also discloses recovered automata materials, arcane holds, and the uncertain status of founts. She reveals that Kit is a living dimension able to consume other spaces, and Banfast accepts responsibility for Rob and five founts while deciding their treatment. Constructionists examine Kit and find it damaged, then attempt to reinforce it. Holly prevents Tala from using a reinscribing device before refinement and begins coordinating a safe preparation plan. Tala resumes exercise, iron practice, and ordinary social contact while experts study how to stabilize her altered body. When constructionists open crates of reinforcement materials around Kit, the sanctum begins an uncontrolled void-powered reaction. The chapter closes with the attempted reinforcement still a dimensional emergency.

Kit absorbs magical containment crates and reproduces their stabilizing structures, convincing Constructionist Guild examiners that the sanctum is a living being able to incorporate magical methods. Plans emerge for researchers or a household to work inside it, though teleportation and safety remain unresolved. Ingrit converts demand for Tala's arcane knowledge into money, favors, and expert access. Tala pays her entire debt, an emotional release tied to the circumstances of her capture. Holly updates her inscriptions and keeps refinement on a cautious schedule while Tala rebuilds her strength and learns finer control of her internal iron. Research connects Tala's void sight to her soulbound weapon, and Kit demonstrates that it can relocate a consenting person within itself. Tala begins trauma therapy and recounts her capture, enforced identity, and return. Her therapist urges her to stop isolating the false persona created during captivity. With Alat's help, Tala confronts that construct, forgives it as another victim of manipulation, and dismisses it. The mental partition collapses, leaving Tala to experience the contained memories and emotions directly. Integration has begun, but its immediate cost is severe.

Recovered arcane knowledge produces both promising research and a fatal illegal automaton experiment. Tala completes the integration of her imposed captive identity, then works with Alat on fully sensory simulated training. She upgrades her archive link for effectively unlimited ordinary range and, with Lynn, invokes an incapacity clause that removes all fifty-one remaining Caravan Guild trips. Free of that obligation, Tala begins planning a mobile home and a life chosen on her own terms. Lynn advances to Fused. An expert Archon explains theories about reality beasts, Zeme, the fractured-reality region, void magic, and why human and arcane powers remain in an uneasy balance. Cazor then tests Tala's control of owned iron. Within her aura it behaves like part of her, but iron dragged beyond that boundary ceases to be hers and tears at the bond. Holly finds the test exposed dangerous damage. Rather than merging the Doskanok further into Tala's body, specialists join its bond to her soulbound weapon. Tala selects a configuration that leaves her body unchanged, lets the weapon supply protective iron, and allows lost iron to be consumed by void instead of violently relinquished. The merger succeeds and clears a major obstacle to refinement.

After the weapon and Doskanok bond settle, Tala enters Holly's irreversible refining apparatus. The transformation succeeds, removing conceptual corruption, but the pain and confinement leave Tala weak and traumatized. Holly confirms that Tala is now Refined, with greater magical capacity, physical ability, resistance to disease and poison, and no ordinary age-related decline. Advancement toward Paragon will require a change in her mortal perspective that she does not yet understand. While recovering, Tala meets Simon and Petra, a married pair considering work inside Kit with their children. Lynn learns of Tala's refinement and shares the unresolved loss of her own family. A Constructionist Guild specialist designs a morphic sheath so Tala can safely spar with her weapon's new iron-claiming effect. That effect is tied to intended cutting contact and could also emerge through sharp iron formed from Tala's body. Before leaving Banfast, Tala encounters a siphon attacking a building. Another Archon clears civilians while Tala kills the creature by using her weapon's conceptual authority over iron. The victory proves the merged weapon effective, even as Tala remains cautious about its hazards and her unfinished recovery.

Tala disposes of the siphon's corpse and compensates the other Archon who helped rescue civilians. Simon and Petra test life inside Kit with their children, eventually committing to work there once communications, exits, and housing are secure. Petra begins developing meals from magical harvests, while Simon installs an archive interlink and plans durable infrastructure. Tala hires Lynn and her mageling to sell mundane arcane goods and builds reserves for future travel. The Constructionist Guild offers a recovery net that will return Kit to the Guild if Tala dies, in exchange for inheriting the sanctum and its contents. Tala accepts after consulting trusted advisers, protecting Simon and Petra's family from being stranded. Kit receives the recovery net and a grid node, but internal teleportation continues to fail. Petra records her food methods so the work can continue without her. Holly's final assessments clear Tala for unrestricted activity. Tala immediately spars with Rain and finds that refinement has made her much stronger, while Rain's ability to redirect kinetic vectors again makes him a difficult opponent. The first hint of green in Tala's aura also marks a small, uncertain step toward Paragon.

Tala prepares to leave Banfast, speaks with Rain about the burden of her past killings, and demonstrates the reinscriber for Holly. She then travels overland with Terry while Simon, Petra, and their family remain inside Kit. A full iron sheath now reinforces Tala's inscriptions and contains her magical presence, giving her far greater strength and speed when carefully controlled. On the road she finds an elderly mage irreversibly becoming a fount. Tala and Simon record the transformation as the man's body disappears and a flame fount forms. Through void sight, Tala sees a structure of nothingness restraining the fount from moving onward. Her attempt to close it shifts her perception among Zeme, a mysterious dome, and a next world of pure magic that injures her. Tala chooses to send the fount onward rather than claim or stabilize it. The fount vanishes, and Alat's archive record restores memories Tala briefly loses. A specialist can offer only theories about reality, void, magic, and the dome. After recovering, Tala resumes the journey and reaches Marleyweather, where her estranged father is waiting outside the family alchemist shop.

Tala's father asks her to discourage two younger siblings from entering the academy and accepts responsibility for past decisions that harmed her. Tala refuses to deceive the twins. She gathers her siblings inside Kit, makes clear that she still claims them as family, and maintains her separation from her parents' household. Her eldest sister is studying magical theory with a healer-mage and developing an iron-paint business; she later chooses him as her prospective master. Tala spends weeks with her siblings and supports the twins' decision after giving them a realistic account of magehood. She also begins mapping the inactive mature automaton retained in Kit. Terry, carrying grief from the loss of his own flock, subjects Tala to a serious spar meant to decide their future. Tala develops a persistent working that makes local reality harder to manipulate, but Terry defeats her. The twins leave together for the academy. Terry then explains that he has chosen to stay and test whether he and Tala can become a flock, without accepting a soul bond. Simon begins monitoring Tala's unexplained reality-stabilizing working. Tala leaves Marleyweather without resolving whether she will accept her father's offer of future support.

While traveling back toward Banfast, Tala accepts a commission to inspect a mountain valley containing authorized founts. An upland tiger attacks and proves able to draw immense power from the terrain and regenerate major injuries almost instantly. Tala cannot use her most destructive options without violating the commission's limits, and a new iron defense demands too much concentration under the tiger's attacks. Terry joins the fight, then signals retreat when their efforts fail. Tala trusts him and withdraws, leaving the tiger alive for another Archon to address. In Banfast, Tala shares a farewell dinner with Lynn and Lynn's mageling before moving her base to the city where Rain is based. She plans to maintain those friendships and return after several months. Cazor meets her in a reinforced arena for another iron test. His opposed magnetic poles can pull surface iron away when Tala concentrates only on holding it, exposing a limit in her defense. Tala answers by extending her aura through iron tendrils and crushing the poles. She ends the book Refined, free of her caravan obligations, partnered with Terry as a prospective flock, connected to her human allies, and relocating while major questions about founts, Kit, her iron bond, and Paragon advancement remain open.

characters.description: A girl of the Ghalas-at people who lives with her community on a small island off the California coast. Alert, capable, and strongly attached to her younger brother Ramo, she watches an unfamiliar hunting ship enter the harbor and senses danger in its arrival.
characters.name: Karana

characters.description: Karana's energetic younger brother. His curiosity and pride often outrun his judgment, and he is eager to be treated as more grown-up than he is.
characters.name: Ramo

characters.description: Karana's father and the chief of Ghalas-at. He negotiates with Captain Orlov over payment for the sea otters the visitors intend to hunt and remains wary of their promises.
characters.name: Chowig

characters.description: The Russian captain of a ship carrying Aleut hunters. He bargains with Chowig for permission to hunt sea otters around the island, but the arrangement places the islanders and the visitors in an uneasy confrontation.
characters.name: Captain Orlov

characters.description: Karana's older sister, who shares the islanders' work and later boards the rescue ship with the surviving community.
characters.name: Ulape

characters.description: A respected man who becomes chief after the Aleut hunters' departure leaves the village devastated. He sets out alone for a country across the sea, hoping to find a safer home and send help back for his people.
characters.name: Kimki

characters.description: The leader of the island's wild dog pack, larger and more formidable than the others. Karana recognizes him as an Aleut dog left behind after the hunters' visit and regards him as her chief enemy.
characters.name: Rontu

characters.description: A young sea otter Karana finds wounded after hunters return to the island's waters. She brings food while the animal heals and gives it a name, beginning another of the bonds that ease her isolation.
characters.name: Mon-a-nee

characters.description: A young Aleut girl who comes ashore while another hunting party is camped on the island. Though Karana initially hides from her as an enemy, Tutok approaches with friendly curiosity and the two cautiously exchange words and gifts.
characters.name: Tutok

characters.description: A young wild dog whose appearance reminds Karana of Rontu. She captures and tames him during her later years on the island and names him for that resemblance.
characters.name: Rontu-Aru

recaps.ending: After many years alone, Karana sees a ship whose men have come to take her away. She prepares the clothing expected by the strangers, gathers the possessions she can carry, and leaves the island with Rontu-Aru and her birds. On the voyage she learns why no one returned for her: the ship that carried the Ghalas-at away later sank, and the knowledge that she had remained behind was lost. Karana reaches the California mission settlements after eighteen years of solitude. Her departure closes her life on the island without undoing its losses; she carries with her the skills, memories, and affection for animals that sustained her there.
recaps.in_short: Karana lives with the Ghalas-at on an island off California until a dispute with visiting Aleut sea-otter hunters kills most of the community's men. A rescue ship later takes the survivors away, but Karana jumps overboard when her brother Ramo is left behind. Wild dogs kill Ramo, leaving her alone. She builds a home, makes weapons despite tribal prohibitions, gathers food, and abandons a dangerous attempt to reach the mainland. Her effort to destroy the wild dogs changes when she nurses their wounded leader and names him Rontu; he becomes her companion. Karana also cares for birds and an otter, and she befriends an Aleut girl named Tutok during a later hunting visit. Rontu eventually dies, and Karana tames a younger dog, Rontu-Aru. After eighteen years a ship finally finds her. She leaves with her animals and learns that the ship carrying her people had sunk, preventing anyone from returning for her.

recaps.text: A ship arrives at the Island of the Blue Dolphins, home of Karana and the Ghalas-at people. Its captain, Orlov, leads Aleut hunters who want the island's valuable sea otters. Karana's father, Chief Chowig, agrees that the visitors may hunt in exchange for an equal share of the catch, but both sides remain suspicious. When Orlov prepares to sail without giving the islanders what they believe they are owed, the dispute becomes a battle on the beach. The hunters escape, but Chowig and many other Ghalas-at men are killed. The surviving community, now made up largely of women and children, must reorganize its life under Kimki's leadership while guarding against another attack.

After the devastating fight with the Aleut hunters, Kimki leaves the island to find a safer country. Much later a ship arrives to collect the Ghalas-at. During the hurried departure, Karana discovers that her younger brother Ramo has been left ashore. She jumps from the ship and swims back rather than abandon him. The ship cannot return in the rising storm, and the two children expect it to come back soon. Ramo declares himself chief and goes out alone, but the island's wild dogs attack and kill him. Karana is now the only person left on the island. Grief turns to anger, and she burns the abandoned village before beginning the work of keeping herself alive.

Alone after Ramo's death, Karana makes weapons even though her people's customs discouraged women from doing so. She chooses a defensible place for a house, fences it with whale ribs, stores food, and protects herself from the wild dogs. Hoping to reach the mainland, she launches an old canoe, but leaks and rough water force her to turn back. The island, once a place she only wanted to escape, becomes the home she must understand and maintain. Karana hunts the dog pack and wounds its large leader. When she finds him helpless, however, she cannot finish killing him. She carries him home, feeds him, and names him Rontu. The animal that had represented her anger becomes her companion.

Karana and Rontu settle into a shared life. She improves her shelter, explores the island, and survives dangerous encounters at sea and along the cliffs. Her relationship with the island's animals changes: she rescues a wounded young otter, Mon-a-nee, and treats birds and other creatures as companions rather than merely resources. When Aleut hunters return, Karana hides her canoe and moves into a cave so that she will not be discovered. The visit revives memories of the attack that destroyed her community and makes any contact with the newcomers seem dangerous.

While hiding from the returning hunters, Karana meets Tutok, a young Aleut girl. Karana is wary and initially conceals her identity, but the girls gradually exchange words, food, and small gifts. Their friendship gives Karana brief human companionship without erasing the danger associated with the hunting party. Tutok eventually sails away with her people, leaving Karana alone again. The seasons continue. Rontu grows old and dies, and Karana buries the companion who transformed her relationship with the wild dogs. Later she captures a dog that resembles him and names it Rontu-Aru. Earthquakes and a great wave alter parts of the island, but Karana repairs the damage and continues waiting.

A ship finally anchors near the island, and this time Karana is able to make contact with the men who come ashore. She dresses and prepares herself to leave, gathers what she can take, and boards with Rontu-Aru and her birds. The island has sustained her through eighteen years of solitude, but the arrival offers the human community she has long waited for. During the voyage Karana learns that the ship which removed the Ghalas-at later sank, taking with it the knowledge that she had remained behind. She reaches the mission settlement in California, carrying her memories of Ramo, Rontu, Tutok, and the island animals into a new life.

characters.description: William 'Bill' Denbrough, an eleven-year-old boy in Derry, Maine, whose severe stutter marks him out but who is the natural leader of his circle of friends. In the autumn of 1957 he is sick in bed when he builds a paper boat for his little brother, Georgie, to sail in the flooded gutters - the last time he sees him alive. Georgie's death breaks something in Bill and in his grieving parents, and his guilt and fury at whatever took his brother drive him to face it. As an adult in 1985 he has become a successful horror novelist living in England, his stutter long gone, when a phone call summons him back to a town he had almost entirely forgotten.
characters.name: Bill Denbrough

characters.description: A malevolent presence beneath the town of Derry, Maine, that preys on the town's children. To Georgie Denbrough it appears from a storm drain as Pennywise the Dancing Clown, a grinning figure in a silver-buttoned suit who charms him close and kills him. It is plainly not human - a shape-shifting predator that makes the drains and sewers of Derry its hunting ground.
characters.name: It

characters.description: George 'Georgie' Denbrough, Bill's six-year-old brother. On a rainy day in October 1957 he chases his paper boat down a flooded street and meets a clown in a storm drain who calls himself Pennywise. His death is the first killing in the creature's new cycle and the loss that sets his brother Bill on a lifelong collision with It.
characters.name: Georgie Denbrough

characters.description: Ben Hanscom, an overweight, bookish, lonely boy newly arrived in Derry and mercilessly bullied for his size. Clever and gentle, with a gift for building and design, he finds his first real friends among the outcasts who will name themselves the Losers' Club, and quietly falls in love with Beverly Marsh. As an adult he has become a lean, celebrated architect, the fat boy remade almost past recognition, when the call comes to return.
characters.name: Ben Hanscom

characters.description: Beverly Marsh, the only girl in the Losers' Club, a brave and quick-tempered redhead growing up poor under a violent, controlling father. Loyal and the best shot among them with a slingshot, she is the object of both Ben's and Bill's affection. As an adult she becomes a fashion designer trapped in a marriage to an abusive husband that grimly echoes her childhood.
characters.name: Beverly Marsh

characters.description: Eddie Kaspbrak, a small, anxious boy convinced by his smothering, hypochondriac mother that he is chronically ill; he clutches an asthma inhaler he treats as a lifeline. Braver than he believes and fiercely loyal, he is a steadfast member of the Losers. As an adult he runs a limousine company and has married a woman much like his mother.
characters.name: Eddie Kaspbrak

characters.description: Richard 'Richie' Tozier, a wisecracking, bespectacled boy who cannot stop talking, forever slipping into funny voices and comic 'Voices' routines that get him into trouble. His humour masks real fear and real courage. As an adult he becomes a successful radio disc jockey in California.
characters.name: Richie Tozier

characters.description: Mike Hanlon, one of the few Black children in Derry and the last to join the Losers' Club. Steady and thoughtful, he alone stays in the town as an adult, becoming its librarian and the group's self-appointed watchman. When the killings begin again in 1985, it is Mike who recognises the pattern and makes the phone calls that summon the others home.
characters.name: Mike Hanlon

characters.description: Stanley Uris, a neat, orderly, rational boy who loves birds and dislikes disorder, and the member of the group least able to accept the impossible thing they face. As an adult he is a prosperous accountant in Atlanta. When Mike's call reaches him and the buried memories start to return, the prospect of confronting It again proves more than he can bear.
characters.name: Stan Uris

characters.description: Henry Bowers, a vicious older teenager who leads a gang that terrorises the younger children, and who is tormented in turn by his own brutal, unstable father. His cruelty toward the Losers escalates from beatings into something murderous, and It works on his madness like a tool.
characters.name: Henry Bowers

characters.description: Audra Phillips, a film actress and Bill Denbrough's wife, who knows almost nothing of his childhood in Derry. When Bill abruptly leaves England to answer Mike's call, she follows him to America, walking unknowing into the town's danger.
characters.name: Audra Phillips

characters.description: An immense, benign cosmic being, ancient beyond reckoning, glimpsed by the children in a shared vision of It's arrival on Earth long before humanity. The Turtle is presented as a counterweight to It within a wider order of things - vast, weary, and largely detached from human affairs, yet the source of a faint help the children can draw on against the creature that hunts them.
characters.name: The Turtle

recaps.ending: It ends with the ancient creature destroyed for good. In its lair beneath Derry the Losers who made the final descent - Bill, Ben, Beverly and Richie - crush It's heart and destroy the eggs it had laid to perpetuate itself, breaking the centuries-old cycle of killings. The reckoning costs them dearly. Stanley Uris took his own life rather than return. Henry Bowers, broken out of the asylum and driven by It, gravely wounded Mike Hanlon, who survives in the hospital, and was then killed by Eddie Kaspbrak in self-defence. And in the lair itself the creature mortally wounded Eddie, tearing off his arm as he attacked it to save his friends; he died in the tunnels. As the thing dies, a violent storm brings down Derry's old downtown, which sinks into the flooding canals. Bill's wife, Audra, drawn into danger after following him from England, is left catatonic; Bill brings her back to herself in a final echo of the childhood magic they had used. With the evil gone, the deep bond and shared memory that had held the friends together - in 1958 and again in 1985 - begins once more to dissolve. The survivors leave Derry and return to their separate adult lives, and their recollection of the town, of the creature, and of each other fades almost entirely away, closing the story on the same note of forgetting on which the town has always run.
recaps.in_short: In 1957 the town of Derry, Maine loses six-year-old Georgie Denbrough to a clown in a storm drain - the first killing in a new cycle of an ancient, shape-shifting evil that wakes every twenty-seven years to feed on the town's children. The following summer, Georgie's brother Bill and six other bullied outcasts form the Losers' Club, face the creature in its many personalised forms, wound it in the sewers, and swear to return if it ever comes back. Twenty-seven years later, in 1985, the killings resume, and Mike Hanlon - the one who stayed - calls the others home. Now prosperous adults who had forgotten almost everything, they reunite; one, Stan, chooses death over returning. Henry Bowers, sprung from an asylum and driven by It, gravely wounds Mike and is killed by Eddie Kaspbrak in self-defence. The rest descend again beneath Derry, where the creature itself mortally wounds Eddie, and they destroy It by crushing its heart and its eggs. The town's old centre collapses as the thing dies. The survivors leave Derry alive but, as before, their memories of the horror and of one another gently fade away for good.

recaps.text: In October 1957, in the small city of Derry, Maine, a sick ten-year-old named Bill Denbrough makes a paper boat for his little brother, Georgie. Georgie chases it through the rain-flooded streets until it slips into a storm drain, where a clown who calls himself Pennywise is waiting. The clown lures him close and kills him. Georgie's death is the first in a new wave of child killings and disappearances, though the adults of Derry seem strangely unwilling to see the pattern. It marks the return, after decades of sleep, of an ancient predatory thing that has fed on the town's children for centuries.

The story moves to 1985. A brutal killing - the murder of a young man named Adrian Mellon, thrown from a bridge - tells Mike Hanlon, now Derry's librarian and the only member of his childhood circle still living in town, that the evil has woken again on its roughly twenty-seven-year cycle. As children in 1958, Mike and six friends had faced the creature, wounded it, and sworn a blood oath to return and finish it if it ever came back. Mike makes six phone calls. One by one the others - Bill Denbrough, Ben Hanscom, Beverly Marsh, Eddie Kaspbrak, Richie Tozier and Stan Uris - feel an old, half-buried dread return as they are summoned home. All have prospered, and all have forgotten almost everything. Stanley Uris, unable to face it, takes his own life rather than go back.

The narrative begins moving between the adults' 1985 return and their childhood summer of 1958. In flashback the friends are introduced as lonely, bullied children: Bill grieving Georgie and fighting his stutter; overweight, gentle Ben Hanscom, new in town; anxious Eddie with his inhaler; loudmouthed Richie; brave Beverly, the only girl, growing up under a violent father; and rational Stan. Each has already had a private, terrifying encounter with the thing that wears many faces - Pennywise the clown chief among them - and each has learned that in Derry the monster reaches into your own fears and takes their shape. Drawn together as outcasts, the children begin to form the group that will call itself the Losers' Club.

Through the summer of 1958 the Losers' Club comes fully together, its seventh member the thoughtful Mike Hanlon, one of the few Black children in town and a target of the same bullies. Building a dam in the marshy Barrens becomes the ground of their friendship. Their encounters with It sharpen and multiply, each child menaced by a personalised horror, and a confrontation at the derelict house on Neibolt Street shows them the creature can be hurt and driven off when they stand together. They come to understand they are facing a single ancient being that has preyed on Derry's children for generations while the adults look away. Meanwhile Henry Bowers and his gang hunt the Losers with growing, unnatural viciousness.

In 1985 the surviving friends reconvene in Derry. Gathering for a reunion dinner, their long-blank memories come flooding back, along with fresh manifestations of It that only they can see. Mike lays out for them the town's hidden history: a recurring cycle of massacres, fires and disappearances stretching back centuries, each coinciding with the creature's waking. As the adults commit to finishing what they began as children, It senses the threat and moves against them, engineering the escape of Henry Bowers - now a grey, broken man locked in an asylum - and setting him loose to hunt the Losers once more.

The 1958 storyline reaches high summer. An escalating feud with Henry Bowers' gang culminates in the 'apocalyptic rockfight,' a pitched battle in the Barrens that the Losers win, cementing them as a group. Seeking to understand their enemy, they perform a ritual in a smoke-hole and share a vision reaching back to the deep past: they glimpse It arriving on Earth from the void ages before humanity, and sense a vast opposing presence, a Turtle, that hints they are not entirely without help. The bonds among the children deepen, including the tangled affections between Beverly, Bill and Ben, as they realise they will have to go down into the dark after the thing themselves.

The children resolve to hunt It in its lair beneath the town, reached through the sewers and drains where it moves. They melt down silver to make slugs for Beverly's slingshot, their best weapon of faith and improvisation. Descending into the tunnels, they find and wound the creature, driving it back into deeper hibernation without killing it. Lost and coming apart in the dark afterward, they hold together through an act that binds the group and lets them find their way out. Battered but alive, the seven swear a blood oath: if It ever returns, they will come back to Derry and end it for good. Then they climb back into the daylight and, over the years, begin to forget.

It moves against the reunited Losers through Henry Bowers, now a grey, broken man whom the creature springs from the asylum and drives back to Derry as its weapon. Henry attacks Mike Hanlon at the library by night and wounds him gravely; Mike barely survives and is left in the hospital, out of the fight that follows. Henry then comes for Eddie Kaspbrak at the Derry Town House, and in the struggle Eddie kills him, coming away with a broken arm. Knowing the creature will pick them off one by one if they hesitate, the remaining friends - Bill, Ben, Beverly, Richie and the injured Eddie - descend into the sewers beneath the town to finish It for good.

The Losers reach It in its lair and find that its physical form is closest to an enormous spider, though its true nature lies beyond the physical, in a searing light the survivors call the deadlights. Bill Denbrough confronts the creature mind to mind in the Ritual of Chud, a contest of wills that carries him beyond the edge of the universe, where he senses the vast, benign Turtle and the greater order in which both It and its opponents exist. It is a battle fought as much in thought and courage as in the body, and it brings Bill face to face with the thing that killed his brother.

The Losers destroy It. In the lair the creature, in its monstrous spider form, mortally wounds Eddie Kaspbrak, tearing off his arm as he attacks it to save Bill and Richie; he bleeds to death in the dark among his friends. The others find and crush the creature's heart, and destroy the clutch of eggs it had laid to continue its kind, ending the cycle for good. As It dies, a great storm tears through Derry and its old downtown collapses into the flooding waterways. Bill, Ben, Beverly and Richie climb out alive, and Mike recovers in the hospital from Henry Bowers' attack; of the seven who swore the oath, Eddie and Stan are gone. Bill's wife, Audra, who had followed him to Derry, is left catatonic by an encounter with It; in a last act tied to their childhood, Bill revives her. With the creature gone, the survivors' memories of Derry and of one another once again begin to fade, this time permanently, as they leave the town and return to their separate lives - free at last, and no longer remembering the friends who made them so.

characters.description: A large dog raised on a California estate, then stolen and sold into Klondike sled service. Intelligent, proud, and physically powerful, Buck must adapt quickly when comfort is replaced by hard labor and violence.
characters.name: Buck

characters.description: An experienced government courier who buys Buck for northern sled work and recognizes his unusual quality.
characters.name: Perrault

characters.description: Perrault's companion and the capable driver who teaches Buck the work and discipline of a sled team.
characters.name: François

characters.description: The experienced white lead dog of François's team. Spitz quickly identifies Buck as a rival and defends his authority through intimidation and force.
characters.name: Spitz

characters.description: A seasoned outdoorsman who encounters Buck after an inexperienced party has driven its sled team to exhaustion. He sees the dog's condition and intervenes against further abuse.
characters.name: John Thornton

characters.description: A wolf-dog who helps lure sled dogs away from two starving men traveling through the northern wilderness. She is cautious, intelligent, and closely tied to the wild pack shadowing them.
characters.name: Kiche

characters.description: A gray wolf who pairs with Kiche after the famine. Scarred by earlier conflicts but experienced and resourceful, he helps provide for her when she makes a den.
characters.name: One Eye

characters.description: Kiche's gray cub, born in a wilderness den during a time of scarcity. More vigorous and inquisitive than his littermates, he gradually learns the boundaries of the den and the laws of hunger and danger outside it.
characters.name: White Fang

characters.description: An Indigenous man who recognizes Kiche as the offspring of a wolf and a dog once owned by his family. He claims both her and her cub when they enter his camp and gives the cub his name.
characters.name: Gray Beaver

characters.description: A puppy in Gray Beaver's camp who immediately attacks the inexperienced White Fang. Lip-lip's persistent persecution helps isolate the young wolf-dog from the other dogs.
characters.name: Lip-lip

characters.description: A cruel white man at Fort Yukon who becomes determined to own White Fang. He exploits Gray Beaver's weakness for alcohol to gain control of the animal.
characters.name: Beauty Smith

characters.description: A visiting mining engineer who sees White Fang trapped in a brutal dogfight and stops the contest. Scott is appalled by the animal's treatment and takes responsibility for him.
characters.name: Weedon Scott

characters.description: Weedon Scott's experienced dog driver. Matt helps care for White Fang and approaches the suspicious animal with patience and practical caution.
characters.name: Matt

characters.description: Weedon Scott's father, a retired judge living with the Scott family in California. He doubts that White Fang can safely adapt to the household but judges the animal by what he does rather than by appearance alone.
characters.name: Judge Scott

recaps.ending: The collection closes with White Fang established at Weedon Scott's California home. He has learned the rules of domestic life, made peace with the sheepdog Collie, and earned the family's trust. The escaped convict Jim Hall enters the house to kill Judge Scott, whose courtroom sentence he blames for his imprisonment. White Fang fights Hall and saves the household, suffering gunshot wounds and severe fractures. A surgeon gives him little chance, but he survives a long recovery. Outside, Collie leads him to their puppies. The family now calls him the Blessed Wolf, and the once-isolated fighter rests safely among his offspring. This conclusion reverses the direction of the collection's first story: Buck leaves human society for the wolf pack after Thornton's death, while White Fang travels from the wild into a lasting human and canine family.
recaps.in_short: The collection follows two powerful dogs moving in opposite directions across the boundary between domestic life and the wild. In The Call of the Wild, Buck is stolen from California, becomes a dominant Klondike sled dog, and is rescued from abusive owners by John Thornton. When raiders kill Thornton, Buck avenges him and joins a wolf pack, becoming a legendary wild leader. White Fang begins with a wolf-dog cub born during a northern famine. Claimed by Gray Beaver, he grows isolated and fierce under attacks from other dogs, then is sold to Beauty Smith and forced to fight. Weedon Scott rescues him and patiently earns his trust. White Fang follows Scott to California, adapts to family life, and nearly dies saving Judge Scott from an escaped convict. He recovers and joins Collie beside their puppies, fully accepted as the family's Blessed Wolf.

recaps.text: In The Call of the Wild, Buck is stolen from Judge Miller's California estate and sold north as demand grows for sled dogs. A dog breaker teaches him the power of the club, and the couriers Perrault and François put him to work in the Klondike. Buck learns the harsh rules of trail life, challenges the lead dog Spitz, and eventually kills him. He takes command of the team and proves an exceptional leader, but repeated mail runs wear the dogs down. The team is then sold to Hal, Charles, and Mercedes, whose inexperience and cruelty push it toward destruction.

John Thornton prevents Hal from beating the collapsed Buck and keeps him when the travelers continue onto unsafe river ice and perish. Buck recovers and becomes devoted to Thornton, saving his life and performing feats that fund a remote prospecting journey. Yet he also ranges into the forest for longer periods. After Yeehat raiders kill Thornton and destroy the camp, Buck attacks them and then joins a wolf pack. He becomes its leader and a feared legend while continuing to visit the site of Thornton's death. The Call of the Wild ends with Buck fully returned to wild life.

White Fang opens during a northern famine. Bill and Henry struggle to carry a coffin toward safety while a wolf pack follows their dwindling sled team. A strangely doglike she-wolf lures their animals away one by one. Bill pursues her and is killed; Henry survives only until rescuers arrive. With food eventually more plentiful, the she-wolf, Kiche, mates with an older wolf called One Eye. She makes a den and gives birth. Hunger eliminates most of the litter, leaving one vigorous gray cub whose life is still confined to the dim shelter.

The gray cub explores beyond the den, learning through pain, prey, and predators. One Eye is killed by a lynx; Kiche later kills the lynx but is badly hurt. The cub encounters people and instinctively senses their power. Gray Beaver recognizes Kiche, once connected to his family, and claims her and the cub, naming him White Fang. Camp life brings a new form of hardship: the puppy Lip-lip repeatedly attacks White Fang, while the other dogs join in. White Fang becomes solitary, defensive, and cunning. When Kiche is traded away, his dependence on Gray Beaver deepens despite the man's stern rule.

White Fang adapts to human ownership and becomes a formidable sled leader. His isolation lets him dominate the dogs that once tormented him, and during a famine he survives alone before returning to Gray Beaver. At Fort Yukon, Beauty Smith wants him and repeatedly supplies Gray Beaver with alcohol until the man sells. White Fang resists and escapes, but Gray Beaver returns him. Beauty Smith keeps him chained, provokes him for spectators, and turns him into a professional fighting animal. Constant cruelty intensifies White Fang's hatred and leaves him almost unable to tolerate contact.

A bulldog named Cherokee nearly kills White Fang in a staged fight. Weedon Scott and his driver Matt stop the contest, force Beauty Smith to surrender the animal, and nurse White Fang. Patient treatment gradually teaches him that a person can offer care rather than pain. White Fang becomes intensely attached to Scott, defends him, and suffers when Scott leaves temporarily. When Scott prepares to return to California, White Fang escapes confinement and reaches the departing boat. Scott accepts the strength of that bond and takes him south.

At the Scott family estate in California, White Fang learns not to attack livestock or household animals and slowly wins over the family. Collie, the resident sheepdog, remains wary but later becomes his mate. Jim Hall, an escaped convict seeking revenge on Judge Scott, breaks into the house at night. White Fang attacks Hall and saves the judge, but is shot and badly injured. Despite grave wounds, he survives. Once recovered, he is brought outside to Collie and their puppies. The family calls him the Blessed Wolf, and he rests among the pups as a trusted member of a secure home.

characters.description: The eldest of the three Kaul grandchildren and the Pillar, or head, of the No Peak clan, one of the two great jade-wearing families of Janloon. He inherited the position young, when his grandfather stepped back, and governs by patience and persuasion rather than force, weighing every decision against what the clan can afford to lose. He is widely respected and privately unsure of himself, permanently measured against a legendary predecessor, and he carries the quiet humiliation of a marriage that ended when his wife left him. A highly capable Green Bone, he would rather settle a problem with a negotiation than a blade.
characters.name: Kaul Lanshinwan

characters.description: The middle Kaul sibling and the Horn of No Peak, the clan's military leader, responsible for its Fists and Fingers and for answering any insult to the family. Charming, quick-tempered and physically formidable, he is adored by the young warriors under his command and feared by everyone else in Janloon. He is fiercely loyal to his brother Lan even when he disagrees with him, and settles problems with immediate action where Lan would deliberate. He is involved with Maik Wen, the sister of his two closest lieutenants, a relationship his family does not approve of.
characters.name: Kaul Hiloshudon

characters.description: The youngest Kaul sibling, returning to Janloon after two years in Espenia, where she studied business and lived with a foreign boyfriend. She left Kekon after quarrelling with her grandfather and gave up her jade before going, an act the clan treats as close to desertion. Trained at the same academy as her brothers and gifted at both jade abilities and analysis, she wants an ordinary professional life outside the family business and resists every attempt to draw her back into it.
characters.name: Kaul Shaelinsan

characters.description: The Kaul grandfather, founder of the No Peak clan and a national hero of the war that drove the Shotarian occupation off Kekon, which he led alongside his old comrade Ayt Yugontin. Age and illness have worn him down; he no longer runs the clan but still expects to be obeyed, and his interference repeatedly undercuts his grandson Lan. He is devoted to his oldest adviser and openly disappointed in his granddaughter.
characters.name: Kaul Seningtun

characters.description: The Weather Man of No Peak, in charge of the clan's businesses and finances, and Kaul Sen's closest adviser for decades. Elderly, softly spoken and habitually secretive, he keeps his own counsel and his own arrangements, and treats the younger Kauls as children who have not earned their positions. Lan and Hilo both distrust him, and his sympathies toward Kekon's former occupiers are an old source of suspicion, but he is protected by the grandfather's loyalty.
characters.name: Yun Dorupon

characters.description: A cousin taken into the Kaul household as a boy after his mother's death, now in his final year at Kaul Dushuron Academy, the clan's training school for Green Bones. He is half Espenian, which shows in his face and marks him as an outsider in Janloon, and he is unusually gifted with jade, enough that his teachers expect great things of him. He is also frightened of it: his mother was a Green Bone who lost her mind and her life to jade overexposure, and he does not know whether the same is waiting for him. He is devoted to Lan and Hilo, who raised him, and privately unsure he wants the life the clan has planned for him.
characters.name: Emery Anden

characters.description: Hilo's girlfriend and the sister of the Maik brothers who serve as his lieutenants. She is a stone-eye, born unable to perceive or bear jade at all, a condition Kekonese custom treats as unlucky and shameful; because of it she can never be a Green Bone and is considered an unsuitable match for the Horn of a clan. Practical, composed and quietly ambitious for the family, she manages the household and its social obligations and understands Janloon's politics better than most of the men who make it.
characters.name: Maik Wen

characters.description: The elder Maik brother and Hilo's chief Fist, a broad, unhurried man with exceptional Perception. The Maiks' father disgraced the family name, and Hilo took the brothers in when no other clan would have them, so their loyalty to him is absolute. Kehn handles the daily discipline and deployment of the Horn's men.
characters.name: Maik Kehn

characters.description: The younger Maik brother, wiry and volatile, who does the work the clan does not discuss: killings arranged quietly and without ceremony. He is devoted to Hilo without reservation and takes more pleasure in violence than his brother does.
characters.name: Maik Tar

characters.description: The Pillar of the Mountain clan, No Peak's rival for control of Janloon, and the adopted daughter of the clan's founder Ayt Yugontin. She took the leadership after her father's death in a succession fight with her adoptive brother, and few in either clan believe she came by it cleanly. Disciplined, patient and entirely unsentimental, she is the only woman to lead a great clan and she intends to bring all of Kekon's jade under a single authority, her own.
characters.name: Ayt Madashi

characters.description: The Horn of the Mountain and Ayt Mada's military commander: a heavy, powerful Green Bone known for winning fights by absorbing punishment no one else could survive. He believes in his Pillar's vision of one clan over Kekon and holds the Kaul brothers in open contempt.
characters.name: Gont Asch

characters.description: A jadeless young man from one of Janloon's poor districts, the son of a Green Bone who died before he was born, convinced that jade is owed to him and that one lucky theft would change his life. He opens the book robbing a Green Bone of his jade outside a restaurant under clan protection, and he returns to the same ambition however badly it goes for him.
characters.name: Bero

characters.description: Lan's Pillarman, the aide who manages the Pillar's schedule, security and messages and one of the few people the Pillar speaks to candidly. Steady, discreet and conscientious, he studied alongside the Kauls at the academy and has served Lan since he took the seat.
characters.name: Woon Papidonwa

characters.description: Lan's former wife, who left him and the world of the clans behind. Her departure is a private wound he has never worked through, and she wants nothing further to do with jade, Green Bones or the Kaul family.
characters.name: Eyni

characters.description: A Royal Council politician backed by No Peak in the contest for the chancellorship of Kekon. Genial, heavy-set and thoroughly transactional, he understands that a chancellor holds the office at the pleasure of whichever clan put him in it.
characters.name: Son Tomarho

recaps.ending: No Peak's New Year's Eve offensive against the Mountain's leadership fails to kill Ayt Mada, but it costs her the Horn of her clan: Anden, wearing far more jade than his body can carry, stops Gont Asch's heart with Channeling, and is so badly damaged by the act that he renounces jade permanently, ending the career the clan raised him for. The war between the clans stops from exhaustion rather than resolution. Ayt Mada keeps the Mountain and remains committed to a single unified clan over Kekon. Hilo is confirmed as Pillar of No Peak, with his sister Shae as Weather Man, Maik Kehn as Horn and Maik Tar as his Pillarman, and he announces that he will marry Wen, a stone-eye, over his family's objections. Kaul Sen, estranged from Hilo since the killing of his old Weather Man, is left isolated and failing. The clan has survived, but it has lost its Pillar, the grandfather's blessing, and any illusion that its quarrel with the Mountain can be contained inside Janloon: both clans now have foreign money, foreign buyers and foreign enemies in play, and Kekon's jade has become an international commodity. Bero, the jadeless thief from the opening pages, is still alive and still chasing jade.
recaps.in_short: On the island nation of Kekon, bioenergetic jade gives trained Green Bones superhuman abilities, and the jade trade belongs to the clans. In the capital, Janloon, the Kaul family's No Peak clan is led by Kaul Lan as Pillar and his brother Hilo as Horn. When Ayt Mada, Pillar of the rival Mountain clan, demands that No Peak submit to a single unified clan under her and Lan refuses, the two families slide into open war of street killings, poached businesses and a fight for control of Kekon's government. Lan's sister Shae, home from Espenia, exposes No Peak's own Weather Man as a traitor and is pressed into replacing him. Lan, secretly weakened by a sabotaged supply of the jade drug shine, is ambushed and killed by the Mountain's Horn, Gont Asch. Hilo takes the Pillar's seat and strikes back on New Year's Eve; the attack fails to kill Ayt Mada, but the Kauls' cousin Anden kills Gont with a lethal use of Channeling and is so damaged that he gives up jade forever. The war ends in stalemate: Ayt Mada lives, No Peak survives, and Hilo marries Wen.

recaps.text: Kekon is a small island nation whose mountains hold bioenergetic jade, a mineral that grants trained Kekonese extraordinary abilities: strength, speed, heightened senses, deflection of force and the power to disrupt another body from a distance. Those who wear it are called Green Bones, and the jade trade is controlled by the clans. In the capital, Janloon, two great clans divide the city between them: No Peak, run by the Kaul family, and the Mountain. Both were founded by veterans of the resistance that drove out the Shotarian occupation a generation ago. No Peak's Pillar, its head, is Kaul Lan, the eldest grandson; his younger brother Hilo is the Horn, commanding the clan's warriors; their grandfather Kaul Sen, the war hero who built No Peak, has handed over the title without surrendering his authority, and the clan's businesses are run by his old ally, the Weather Man Yun Dorupon. The book opens with Bero, a jadeless young man from a poor district, robbing a Green Bone of his jade outside the Twice Lucky, a restaurant that pays No Peak for protection, and with Hilo answering the theft in person. Beneath the routine business of tribute payments and protected shops, relations between the two clans are deteriorating, and each is watching the other for weakness.

Kaul Shae, the youngest of the three siblings, comes home to Janloon after two years in Espenia, the wealthy foreign power whose money and culture increasingly shape Kekon. She left after quarrelling with her grandfather and gave up her jade before going, which the clan regards as close to desertion; she now wants an ordinary career and no part in family business, and her brothers cannot understand it. Their cousin Anden, half Espenian and raised in the Kaul house, is in his final year at Kaul Dushuron Academy, the clan's school for Green Bones, where he is the strongest student in his class and privately frightened by what that means. A chance confrontation with Mountain Green Bones at a public festival shows how little goodwill is left between the clans. Ayt Mada, the Mountain's Pillar, then summons Lan to her family's estate and puts a proposal to him directly: the two clans should become one under her leadership, with the Kauls given an honored but subordinate place. She argues that a divided Kekon cannot hold its jade against foreign powers. Lan refuses, and both of them understand what the refusal commits them to.

The Mountain begins taking No Peak apart commercially, poaching its tributary businessmen, the Lantern Men, and pressuring shopkeepers to change allegiance. Lan finds he can get little support from inside his own clan: his grandfather countermands him, and the Weather Man Yun Dorupon treats the clan's finances as private ground. Lan is also concealing a personal problem. He is struggling to carry his jade and suffering the symptoms of overexposure, and he has quietly begun taking SN1, the drug called shine, which raises a wearer's tolerance and which Green Bones consider shameful. Shae takes an outside job but is steadily drawn back toward the clan's difficulties, and her analytical work turns up irregularities in No Peak's accounts. Kekon's entire jade supply is supposed to be mined, refined and distributed under national control; evidence begins to accumulate that jade is being diverted out of that system and off the island, and that people inside the clans know about it.

The rivalry becomes open warfare. Green Bones on both sides settle grievances with clean-bladed duels, and beyond the duels there are ambushes, beatings and killings; Hilo answers every Mountain move at once and escalates. Property is destroyed, and neither clan can back down without losing the loyalty of the people who pay it for protection. Lan is fighting on several fronts at once: against the Mountain, against his grandfather's interference, and against his own worsening condition. Shae is pulled steadily further into the clan's affairs, and her scrutiny of its accounts keeps returning to arrangements the Weather Man has never explained to anyone. The Kauls begin to suspect that some of the damage being done to No Peak is not coming from outside it.

Shae's examination of the clan's finances hardens into proof: Yun Dorupon has been running arrangements he never disclosed, tying No Peak's own Weather Man to jade leaving Kekon and to interests aligned with the country's former occupiers. Lan concludes that he cannot govern the clan while the man remains in place, strips him of the Weather Man's office and turns to Shae to replace him, forcing her to choose between the life she wanted and the clan she was born into. Kaul Sen is enraged at the removal of the friend he has protected for fifty years and turns on his grandsons; the disgraced Weather Man withdraws to a place where clan violence traditionally cannot follow. The street war continues through a typhoon and its aftermath: both clans consolidate territory, mark out which districts and businesses belong to whom, and prepare for something larger than duels. Lan's reliance on shine worsens, and it is noticed by people who can make use of it. His brother and sister both realize that the Pillar has been keeping something from them, and that No Peak's position is considerably weaker than the family has been willing to admit.

Lan goes to the Temple of Divine Return, where the deposed Weather Man has taken sanctuary, meaning to settle the matter himself. Gont Asch, the Horn of the Mountain, is waiting for him. Lan's abilities fail under the strain of the fight, his supply of shine having been tampered with, and Gont kills him and takes his jade. No Peak loses its Pillar without warning. Hilo, who has spent the book as the clan's blunt instrument, becomes head of the family, and the character of the war changes with him: where Lan calculated, Hilo intends to answer a killing with killings. The Kauls are left with grief, a furious and failing grandfather, a leadership in transition, and an enemy who has just demonstrated that she is willing to murder a Pillar.

Hilo takes the Pillar's seat and rebuilds the clan's leadership around people he trusts without reservation: Maik Kehn as Horn, Kehn's brother Tar as his Pillarman, and Shae confirmed as Weather Man. Kaul Sen demands that the disgraced Yun Dorupon be pardoned and left in peace; Hilo has him killed anyway, which ends whatever was left between the new Pillar and his grandfather. The clans then open a second front. The chancellorship of Kekon's Royal Council falls vacant, and each clan works to install its own candidate, since whoever holds the office shapes how the government treats the clans' businesses and their jade. No Peak's man, the councilman Son Tomarho, takes the post. At the academy, Anden finishes first in his class, which means the clan will shortly award him jade, the thing he has spent his life being told he was made for and has come to dread.

Shae uses her foreign education to build relationships for No Peak abroad, reaching toward Espenia's capital and its commercial and political networks, and her work confirms what the accounts had hinted at: the Mountain has been selling Kekonese jade out of the country to foreign buyers, which is both a crime and a betrayal of the national interest that No Peak can use against Ayt Mada. Wen, who as a stone-eye cannot be sensed by any Green Bone's Perception, quietly gathers information the clan could not otherwise reach, and does it without Hilo's permission. With the Mountain overextended and its activities exposed, Hilo assembles a plan to end the war in a single night by removing the people who run the rival clan, and sets it for the New Year.

On New Year's Eve, No Peak strikes at the Mountain's leadership simultaneously across Janloon. The plan does not survive contact: the targets are defended, and the fighting is far bloodier than intended. Anden, who has just graduated and been given the jade he never wanted, is pulled into the worst of it. Confronted by Gont Asch and wearing far more jade than his body can safely carry, he uses Channeling to stop the Horn's heart, killing him. The surge leaves Anden physically wrecked and convinced that jade will destroy him as it destroyed his mother, and he renounces it completely. Gont's death costs the Mountain its military commander and blunts Ayt Mada's campaign, but she survives, keeps her clan, and the war ends in exhaustion rather than victory. Hilo is left the undisputed Pillar of a battered No Peak, with Shae as his Weather Man, and he announces that he will marry Wen despite what the family thinks of the match. Anden, having given up the future the clan trained him for, no longer has a place in it. Bero, still without jade, is alive, unrepentant, and looking for his next opportunity.

characters.description: Pillar of the No Peak clan, in the job for years now and no longer the young Horn who took it after his brother's murder. He still governs by instinct, personal loyalty and a willingness to answer violence immediately, in a Kekon that increasingly rewards lawyers, diplomats and foreign capital instead. He is angry with his wife and his sister over the secret they kept from him, unwilling to say so directly, and unable to stop fighting a war he inherited from his grandfather's generation.
characters.name: Kaul Hiloshudon

characters.description: The Weather Man of No Peak, running the clan's business and political side and, increasingly, its international one. She is the architect of the strategy that tied Kekon to Espenia, and she carries the consequences of it, along with a working relationship with her brother that has gone cold and formal since he learned what she helped his wife do.
characters.name: Kaul Shaelinsan

characters.description: Hilo's wife, a stone-eye who cannot perceive or wear jade, and the mother of his children. The injuries she took working secretly for the clan have left her with lasting damage to her speech and movement, and much of her energy goes into recovering what she can of both. She is undiminished in judgement and in ambition for the family, and unrepentant about what she did.
characters.name: Maik Wen

characters.description: The Kauls' half-Espenian cousin, back in Kekon and wearing jade again after years of refusing it. Rather than take a place among the clan's warriors he is studying medicine, on the conviction that what jade does to the human body is a medical problem that Kekon has never seriously examined. He remains the family member most willing to say uncomfortable things to the Pillar, and he has a life in Espenia he has not closed off.
characters.name: Emery Anden

characters.description: Pillar of the Mountain clan and Hilo's opposite number for the whole of the war. Older now, still without an obvious successor, and still convinced that Kekon can only protect its jade under one clan rather than two. Her strategy of trading with Kekon's enemies has failed expensively, but her position inside her own clan is unshaken and her patience is longer than anyone else's.
characters.name: Ayt Madashi

characters.description: The surviving Maik brother, Wen's sibling and Hilo's most trusted enforcer, responsible for the clan's killings and for the work it does not put in writing. Absolutely loyal to the Pillar and less and less restrained by anything else.
characters.name: Maik Tar

characters.description: Shae's Shadow, the senior aide to the Weather Man, and before that Kaul Lan's Pillarman. Quietly capable and completely dependable, he has served three Kauls in turn and has been in love with the current one for years without saying so usefully.
characters.name: Woon Papidonwa

characters.description: A senior Fist of No Peak: steady, well-liked among the clan's warriors, and more comfortable with the modern, organized shape the clan's military side has been forced into than with the older tradition of duels and personal grudges. As the war drags on he is given increasing responsibility for it.
characters.name: Juen Nu

characters.description: Kaul Lan's son, brought back from Espenia as a small child and raised in the Kaul house by Hilo and Wen alongside their own children. As the son of a Pillar he is treated by the whole clan as the heir to No Peak, a role decided for him before he was old enough to have an opinion about it. He is watchful and serious, aware that he is being measured, and aware that he is the only child in the house who is not Hilo's own.
characters.name: Kaul Niko

characters.description: Hilo and Wen's son, a stone-eye like his mother, which means he will never wear jade or be a Green Bone in a family and a country that measure worth in exactly those terms. Sociable, funny and sharply intelligent, he grows up entirely comfortable with the clan and entirely excluded from the thing it is built around, and he has no intention of accepting that as a limit.
characters.name: Kaul Ru

characters.description: Hilo and Wen's daughter, born with an aptitude for jade and none at all for patience. She is combative from childhood, drawn to the warrior side of the clan, and much more like her father than anyone in the household finds convenient.
characters.name: Kaul Jaya

characters.description: Dauk Losun's Espenian-born son, a lawyer, and Anden's partner from their time together in Port Massy. He belongs to Espenia in a way Anden never will and to Kekon in a way Espenia will never quite let him forget, and the distance between the two countries is the standing problem in their relationship.
characters.name: Dauk Corujon

characters.description: A jadeless man from Janloon who has spent his entire adult life failing to steal his way into greenness, and who has survived every disaster he caused. Bitter, unattached and permanently convinced he is owed something, he drifts toward whoever will use him.
characters.name: Bero

recaps.ending: The clan war that has run through three generations of the Kaul and Ayt families ends. With the Mountain's succession settled in favor of a leader prepared to deal, the two great clans come to terms and stop trying to destroy each other; Kekon's jade industry, its politics and its place among foreign powers all end the book in a shape neither founder would recognize. What cannot be settled by negotiation is settled between Hilo and Ayt Mada personally, at the end of a rivalry that has cost both families almost everything: Ayt Mada dies, and Hilo does not outlive her. The Pillar's seat of No Peak passes to Niko, Kaul Lan's son, who takes it as a decision of his own rather than as the inheritance he was raised to resent, with Shae, Wen, Anden and Jaya around him. The family is smaller than it was, having lost Ru to an anti-clan killing years earlier and having buried much of the generation that started the war, and it is still standing. The book closes on the survivors remembering their dead.
recaps.in_short: Over roughly two decades, the war between No Peak and the Mountain becomes a long, cold struggle fought through business, politics, foreign alliances and assassination while Kekon transforms into a modern country entangled with Espenia. Hilo remains Pillar and Shae Weather Man, slowly repairing a relationship broken by Wen's secret work; Wen recovers what she can from her injuries; Anden becomes a doctor studying jade's effects on the body. The Mountain fields assassins trained in a concealed discipline that hides them from Perception, a jade miners' strike shakes the country, and an anti-clan movement grows into open violence. The next generation grows up: Niko, Lan's son and the reluctant heir; Ru, a stone-eye who builds a public life arguing that jade should not determine a person's worth, and who is murdered for it; and Jaya, a fighter without restraint. Niko leaves the clan and later returns on his own terms. The war finally ends in a settlement with the Mountain's next leader and in a last confrontation between Hilo and Ayt Mada, which neither survives. Niko becomes Pillar of No Peak.

recaps.text: Previously, in Jade City and Jade War: on the island nation of Kekon, bioenergetic jade gives trained Kekonese, called Green Bones, heightened strength, speed and senses, and the jade trade belongs to the clans. In the capital, Janloon, the Kaul family's No Peak clan and Ayt Mada's Mountain clan went to war after Ayt demanded that the two become one under her. No Peak's Pillar, Kaul Lan, was murdered; his brother Hilo took the seat, made their sister Shae his Weather Man, and married Wen, a stone-eye who can neither wear nor be sensed through jade. Their cousin Anden killed the Mountain's Horn with a lethal use of Channeling, renounced jade, and was exiled to Espenia, where he found the Kekonese immigrant community of Port Massy, took up jade again to defend it, and became involved with Dauk Cory. The war then went global: Espenia bought Kekonese jade and the drug that lets foreigners use it, while the Mountain sold jade to Kekon's enemies through the smuggler Zapunyo. No Peak killed Zapunyo, but the operation left Wen seriously and permanently injured, and Hilo discovered that she had been working secretly for the clan with Shae's knowledge. Lan's son Niko was brought back from Espenia to be raised as the clan's heir. Kekon ended the book bound tightly to Espenia, and the two clans ended it still at war.

The clan war has not ended; it has changed shape. No Peak, under Hilo as Pillar with Shae as Weather Man, and the Mountain under Ayt Mada now fight through business, politics, foreign alliances and targeted killing rather than open street battle.
